correctness.rationale: Explicit equations classify six coordinate edges and three diagonals. Their intersections are exactly four ordinary triple axes and nine ordinary double points; normalization has nine rational P1 components and thirteen singular points with thirty branches. The seminormal normalization sequence gives the integral Frobenius module H_1 of the twenty-two-vertex graph and a nine-dimensional torus. Exact spanning-tree cycle matrices give the five characteristic polynomials and explicit finite-group cokernels; each all-extension point-count identity and zeta follows directly from Frobenius-fixed normalization branches. Attached checker replays all integer computations and complete small-prime projective censuses; those tests corroborate and do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The nine-line boundary is the canonical reduced exceptional locus excluded in classical arithmetic height problems on the four-nodal Cayley cubic. Complete connected Picard tori and rational points over every finite extension capture arithmetic gluing beyond known geometric line enumeration, with the three-cycle twist having one rational point although all nine geometric components appear over larger fields. An integral character lattice and finite abelian group presentation give arithmetic information stronger than mere dimension or rational Frobenius eigenvalues.
